newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen A index ends at record high, B shares dip.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen A index ends at record high, B shares dip.

text.p: The Shenzhen A share index closed at a historic high on Wednesday, but failed to lift the B index which eased on profit-taking, analysts said.
The domestic currency A share index rose 8.57 points or 1.63 percent to end at 533.78 on turnover of 21.3 billion yuan. On Tuesday, the A index closed at a record high of 525.21 points.

After recording sharp gains over the last two days, the foreign currency B share index fell 1.46 points or 0.79 percent to end at 182.74. Turnover was HK$233.63 million, compared with HK$263.7 million on Tuesday.
"The A index is rising on optimism over China's economy, fuelled by strongly performing large-capitalisation stocks," an analyst at China Southern Securities said.

China's gross domestic product (GDP) is expected to grow 9.6 percent year-on-year in the first half of 1997, with retail price inflation seen at two percent, an official newspaper said on Tuesday, quoting the State Economic and Trade Commission.
"The B index is still on its way up although it sagged today on profit-taking," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
New listings in Shenzhen scheduled for later this month are now limiting buying of existing listed stocks, brokers said.

Pesticide maker Hubei Sanonda Co Ltd, Shandong Chenming Paper Holdings Ltd and Nanjing Posts & Telecommunications Equipment Co Ltd have all announced they will each offer 100 million B shares for listing later this month.
"Some investors are holding back and waiting for the new shares," the Guotai analyst said.
The new counters are expected to perform well and analysts said they will help boost market sentiment.
"The new listings indicate that the government really is trying to expand the size of the market," the analyst said.
Shenzhen Nanshan Power Station Co Ltd was the sharpest loser in the B share market, dropping HK$0.23 or 4.22 percent to HK$5.22.
On the A share market, Shenzhen Development Bnnk was the most actively traded stock, soaring 4.43 yuan or 9.96 percent to 48.90 yuan on volume of 43 million shares.
